# oxide_system_certificate (Resource)

This resource manages a single TLS certificate for an Oxide silo, which is used
for the silo's console and API endpoints.

Creating a certificate using this resource does not affect other certificates
for the silo, such as those created with the `tls_certificates` attribute of
the `oxide_system_silo` resource.

-> Certificates cannot be updated. Changes to the attributes of this resource
will result in the certificate being destroyed and created anew.

~> To rotate a certificate, first add the new certificate as a separate
`oxide_system_certificate` resource with a different name and apply it. Then
remove the resource for the existing certificate. Replacing a certificate in
place destroys it before its replacement is created, which can leave the silo
without a valid certificate if the replacement is rejected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "oxide_system_certificate" "example" {
  silo_id     = "1fec2c21-cf22-40d8-9ebd-e5b57ebec80f"
  name        = "wildcard-cert-2026"
  description = "Wildcard cert for *.sys.oxide.example.com."
  cert        = file("cert.pem")
  key         = file("key.pem")
  service     = "external_api"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `cert` (String) PEM-formatted string containing public certificate chain.
- `description` (String) Human-readable free-form text about the certificate.
- `key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) PEM-formatted string containing private key. Changes to this attribute alone are not detected, as a new private key requires a new `cert`.
- `name` (String) Unique, immutable, user-controlled identifier of the certificate.
- `service` (String) Service using this certificate.
- `silo_id` (String) ID of the silo that uses the certificate.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique, immutable, system-controlled identifier of the certificate.
- `time_created` (String) Timestamp of when this certificate was created.
- `time_modified` (String) Timestamp of when this certificate was last modified.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is the format `${SILO}/${CERTIFICATE}`, where each part is a name
# or ID.
terraform import oxide_system_certificate.example example-silo/wildcard-cert-2026
```
